                        </ns0:gap> for all such places</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>yell,</ns0:hi> Jer. 51. 38.</ns0:note> shake off <ns0:hi>their fruits</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Are spoiled of their Fruits. Or, as it is rendred in the Margent, and by some others, <ns0:hi>yell</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>roar,</ns0:hi> as this Word is rendred, <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 51. 38.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="10">10. Now will I rise <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">In this extremity, I will appear on the behalf of my People and Land.</ns0:note>, saith the LORD; now will I be exalted, now will I lift up my self.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="11">11. <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 7. 1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> Ye shall conceive chaff, ye shall bring forth stubble <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">In stead of Solid Corn. Your great hopes and de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />signs, O ye <ns0:hi>Assyrians!</ns0:hi> shall be utterly disappointed.</ns0:note>, your breath <ns0:hi>as</ns0:hi> fire shall devour you <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Your Rage against my People shall bring Ruine upon your selves.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="12">12. And the people shall be <ns0:hi>as</ns0:hi> the burnings of lime <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Shall be burnt as easily and effectually, as Chalk is burned to make Lime.</ns0:note>, <ns0:hi>as</ns0:hi> thorns cut up shall they be burnt in the fire.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="13">13. Hear ye <ns0:hi>that are</ns0:hi> far off, what I have done, and ye <ns0:hi>that are</ns0:hi> near, acknowledge my might <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">My power and justice in destroying the <ns0:hi>Assyrians,</ns0:hi> shall be so evident, that People, both far and near, shall be for<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ced to acknowledge it.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="14">14. The sinners in <ns0:hi>Zion</ns0:hi> are afraid <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">This is spoken, not of the <ns0:hi>Assyrians,</ns0:hi> as some would have it, but of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> as appears, both from the Words themselves, and from the following Verses. The Prophet having foretold the Deliverance of God's People, and the Destruction of their Enemies, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 10. 11, 12. for the grea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter Illustration of that wonderful Mercy, here returns to the Description, and gives a lively representation of the dismal and frightful Condition, in which the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> espe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cially such of them as were ungodly and unbelieving, were before this Deliverance came. Although the Godly <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> were, in some measure, supported by the sense of God's Favour, and by God's Promises delivered to them by <ns0:hi>Isaiah<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                        </ns0:hi> yet the generality of the People were filled with Horrors<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and expectation of utter Destruction.</ns0:note>, fearful<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness hath surprized the hypocrites, who among us shall dwell with the devouring fire? who a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mongst us shall dwell with everlasting burn<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ings <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">How shall we be able to abide the Presence, and endure, or avoid the Wrath of that God, who is a consuming Fire; who is now about to destroy us, utterly by the <ns0:hi>Assyrians,</ns0:hi> and will af<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />terward burn us with unquenchable Fire. Fo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> seeing it is sufficiently evident, from both <ns0:hi>Old</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>New-Testament,</ns0:hi> as hath been formerly observed and proved, That the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> except the <ns0:hi>Sadducees,</ns0:hi> did generally believe the rewards and punishments of the future Life; and these Temporal Judg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ments, as they did frequently cut Men off from this Life, so they transmitted them into that future and endless Life: It is not strange, if their guilty Consciences made them dread both the present Judgment here, and the terrible Consequences of it hereafter. Heb. <ns0:hi>Who shall dwell for us,</ns0:hi> &c. <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> in our stead? Who will interpose himself between God's Anger and us. How shall we escape these Miseries? That this is the Sence of this Question, may be gathered from the Answer, given to it in the following Verse; in which, he directs them to the right Course of removing God's Wrath, and regaining His Favour.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="15">15. He that <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 15. 2. & 24. 4.</ns0:note> walketh <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> in righ<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />teousnesses.</ns0:note> righteously <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Who is just in all His dealings with Men, of which the following Clauses explain it: Which is not spoken ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />clusively, as if Piety towards God were not as necessary, as Righteousness towards Men; but comprehensively, this being one Evidence, and a constant companion of Piety.</ns0:note>, and speaketh <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> upright<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nesses.</ns0:note> uprightly <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Who speaks truly and sincerely, what He really intends.</ns0:note>, he that despiseth <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">That refuseth it, not for politick Reasons, as Men some<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />times may do, but from a contempt and abhorrency of in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />justice.</ns0:note> the gains of <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> deceits.</ns0:note> oppressions, that shaketh his hands from holding <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>from taking</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>receiving;</ns0:hi> as this Verb sig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nifies, <ns0:hi>Prov.</ns0:hi> 4. 4. & 5. 5. & 28<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 17. That will not receive, much less retain, Bribes.</ns0:note> of bribes, that stoppeth his ears from hearing of <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> bloods.</ns0:note> blood <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Who will not hearken or as<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sent to any Counsels or Courses, tending to shed innocent Blood.</ns0:note>, and shutteth his eyes from seeing evil <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">That abhorreth the very sight of Sin, commit<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ted by others, and guardeth his Eyes from beholding oc<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />casions of Sin, of which, see on <ns0:hi>Iob.</ns0:hi> 31. 1.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="16">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:596" />16. He shall dwell on <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>heights,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>high places.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> high <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Out of the reach of danger.</ns0:note>, his place of defence <ns0:hi>shall be</ns0:hi> the munitions of rocks, bread shall be given him, his waters <ns0:hi>shall be</ns0:hi> sure <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">God will furnish him with all necessaries.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="17">17. Thine eyes shall see the king <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">First <ns0:hi>Hezekiah,</ns0:hi> and then <ns0:hi>Christ,</ns0:hi> as before.</ns0:note> in his beau<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ty <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Tri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />umphing over all Enemies, and Ruling his own People with Righteousness; in which two things, the beauty and glory of a King and Kingdome, doth chiefly consist.</ns0:note>, they shall behold <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> the land of far distance.</ns0:note> the land that is very far off <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Thou shalt not be shut up in <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> and confined to thine own narrow Borders, as thou hast been, but thou shalt have free Liberty to go abroad with honour and safety, where thou pleasest, even into the remotest Countries, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause of the great renown of thy King, and the enlarge<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment of his Dominions.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="18">18. Thine heart shall meditate terrour <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">This is, Either 1. a Premonition concerning a future Judgment, as if he said, Before these glorious Promises shall be accomplished, thou shalt be brought into great straits and troubles. Or rather 2. a thankful Acknowledgment of deliverance from a former Danger; as if he had said, When thou art delivered, thou shalt, with pleasure and thankful<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> recal to mind thy former Terrours and Miseries.</ns0:note>; <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Cor. 1. 20.</ns0:note> Where <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> the scribe? where <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> the <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> weigher.</ns0:note> re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceiver? where <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> he that counted the tow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ers <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">These Words are, Either 1. words of Gratulation, and Insultation over the Enemy. Thou shalt then say, Where are the great Officers of the <ns0:hi>Assyrian</ns0:hi> Host? They are no where, they are not, they are dead or slain. Or rather 2. the words of Men dismayed and confounded, such as proceeded from the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> in the time of their distress; and are here remembred to aggravate the present Mercy. For the Officers here mentioned, seem not to be those of the <ns0:hi>Assyrian</ns0:hi> Army, who were actually fighting against the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> (for then he would rather have mentioned <ns0:hi>the Captains of the host,</ns0:hi> as the Scripture commonly doth in these cases, than <ns0:hi>the scribes and receivers,</ns0:hi> &c.) but rather of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> who, upon the approach of <ns0:hi>Sen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nacherib,</ns0:hi> began to make Military preparations for the de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fence of the City; and to chuse such Officers, as were necessary and usual, for that end; such as these were, to wit, <ns0:hi>the scribe,</ns0:hi> whom we call <ns0:hi>Muster-Master,</ns0:hi> who was to make and keep a List of the Souldiers, and to call them together, as occasion required: <ns0:hi>The receiver,</ns0:hi> who received and laid out the Money for the Charges of the War; and he <ns0:hi>that counted the Towers,</ns0:hi> who surveyed all the parts of the City, and considered what Towers or Fortifications were to be made or repaired for the Security of the City. And unto these several Officers the People resorted, with great distraction and confusion, to acquaint them with all Oc<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />currences, or to quicken them to their several Works, or to transact Matters with them, as occasion required.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="19">19. <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Kin. 19. 32.</ns0:note> Thon shalt not see a fierce people <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">As <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> said of the <ns0:hi>Egyptians, Exod.</ns0:hi> 14. 13. So I say of the <ns0:hi>Assyrians,</ns0:hi> that fierce and warlike People, whom thou hast seen, with great Terrour, near the Walls of <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> thou shalt see them again no more.</ns0:note>, a <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deu. 28. 49. Jer. 5. 15.</ns0:note> people of a deeper speech than thou canst perceive <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">A forreign Nation, whose Language is abstruse and unknown to thee.</ns0:note>; of a <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                        <ns0:hi>ridicu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lous,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>barba<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rous.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> stammering tongue <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Of which, see on <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 28. 11.</ns0:note>, <ns0:hi>that thou canst</ns0:hi> not understand.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="20">20 Look upon <ns0:hi>Zion</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Contemplate <ns0:hi>Zions</ns0:hi> beauty and safety, and her glo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rious and peculiar Priviledges: It is an Object worthy of thy deepest Meditation.</ns0:note> the city of our solem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nities <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">This he mentions, as the chief part of <ns0:hi>Zions</ns0:hi> Glory and Happiness, that God was solemn<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly Worshipped, and the solemn Assemblies and Feasts kept in her.</ns0:note>, thine eyes shall see <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 46. 5. & 125. 1, 2.</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> a quiet habitation, a tabernacle <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> shall not be taken down, not one of the stakes thereof shall ever be removed, neither shall any of the cords there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />of be broken <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Which was but very obscurely and imperfectly fulfilled in the literal <ns0:hi>Zion;</ns0:hi> but was clearly and fully ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />complished in the mystical <ns0:hi>Zion,</ns0:hi> the Church of God in the times of the Gospel<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> against which, we are assured, that <ns0:hi>the gates of Hell shall not prevail,</ns0:hi> Mat. 16. 18.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="21">21. <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>but there (glorious</ns0:hi> is <ns0:hi>the LORD) we shall have a place,</ns0:hi> &c.</ns0:note> But there <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">In and about <ns0:hi>Zion.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> the glorious LORD <ns0:hi>will be</ns0:hi> unto us a place <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>broad of spaces</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>hands.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> of broad rivers <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> streams <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Though we have nothing but a small and contemptible Brook to defend us; yet God will be as sure and strong a Defence to us, as if we were sur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rounded with such great Rivers, as <ns0:hi>Nilus</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Euphrates,</ns0:hi> which were a great security to <ns0:hi>Egypt</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Babylon.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>, wherein shall go no galley with oars, neither shall gallant ships pass thereby <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">But although they shall have from God, the security of a great River, yet they shall be freed from the disadvantage of it; which is, That the Enemies may come against them in Ships; for no Galleys, nor Ships of the Enemies shall be able to come into this River to annoy them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="22">22. For the LORD <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> our judge <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">To judge for us, to plead our Cause against our Ene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mies, as the ancient Judges of <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> did, <ns0:hi>Iudg.</ns0:hi> 2. 16.</ns0:note>, the Lord <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> our <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Jam. 4. 12.</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> statute<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />maker.</ns0:note> lawgiver <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Our chief Governour, to whom it belongs, to give Laws, and to defend his People.</ns0:note>, the LORD <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> king, he will save us.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="23">23 <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> they have forsaken thy tacklings.</ns0:note> Thy tacklings are loosed <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">He directeth his Speech to the <ns0:hi>Assyrians;</ns0:hi> and having tacitely designed their Army under the notion of a <ns0:hi>gallant Ship, ver.</ns0:hi> 21. he here represents their broken and undone condition, by the Metaphor of a Ship, tossed in a tempe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stuous Sea, having her Cables broken, and all her Tack<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lings loose, and out of order, so as she could have no be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nefit of her Masts or Sails; and therefore is quickly bro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ken, or swallowed up by the Sea.</ns0:note>, they <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">The <ns0:hi>Assyrians,</ns0:hi> of whom he still speaks, as in the first Clause he spake to them.</ns0:note> could not well strengthen their mast, they could not spread the sail: then is the Prey of a great spoil divided, the Iame take the prey <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">They, who came to spoil and prey upon my People, shall become a prey to them, and shall be forced to flee away so suddenly, that they shall leave so many Spoils behind them, that when strong and active Men have carried away all that they desired, there shall be enough left for the Lame, who come last to the Spoil. The ge<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />neral Sence of the place is, That God's People shall be Victorious over all their Enemies.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="24">24. And the inhabitants <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">To wit, of <ns0:hi>Ierusalem;</ns0:hi> God's people.</ns0:note> shall not say, I am sick <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Shall have no cause to complain of any sicknes or calamity; shall be ful<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly delivered from all their Enemies and evil Occurrents; shall enjoy perfect tranquility and prosperity.</ns0:note>: the people that dwell therein shall be forgiven their iniquity <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">This may be added, Either 1. as the Reason of the foregoing pri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viledge; Their Sins, the main causes of all their Distres<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ses, shall be pardoned; and therefore their Sufferings, the effects of Sin, shall cease: Or 2. as an additional Favour. They shall not onely receive from me a glorious Tempo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ral Deliverance; but, which is infinitely better, the par<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />don of all their Sins, and all those spiritual and everlasting Blessings, which attend upon that Mercy.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
